entities.name: Blue Origin

New Glenn reached orbit on its first flight, January 2025
Building the Blue Moon lunar lander for NASA's Artemis programme

entities.name: Firefly Aerospace
entities.does: Alpha launch vehicle and the Blue Ghost lunar lander
notable: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed upright on Mare Crisium in March 2025
Alpha is its small launch vehicle
One of the few commercial landers to reach the Moon intact

entities.name: Hubble
entities.does: Optical and ultraviolet astronomy — still the sharpest UV eye we have
notable: The Deep Field (1995): point at nothing, find thousands of galaxies
Pinned down the expansion rate, and started the tension over its value
Still working after 35 years and five servicing missions

entities.name: IceCube
entities.does: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos
notable: Found the first high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, 2013
Traced one 2017 event back to a flaring blazar
Mapped neutrino emission from the plane of our own galaxy, 2023

entities.name: JWST
entities.does: Infrared astronomy — the earliest galaxies
notable: First images released July 2022
Galaxies seen further back than any telescope had reached
CO2 detected in an exoplanet atmosphere (WASP-39b), a first
The TRAPPIST-1 rocky planets, checked for air

entities.name: LHCb
entities.does: Beauty and charm quark decays — matter/antimatter asymmetry and flavour anomalies

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.does: GPT models
notable: GPT-3 (2020) then ChatGPT (2022), which moved the field into public view
The API most consumer AI products are built on

entities.name: SpaceX
entities.does: Falcon 9 and Starship launch vehicles
notable: Falcon 9: first orbital-class booster landing in 2015, now routine and reflown
Dragon: first commercial crew flight, Demo-2, in 2020
Starship: full flight tests since 2023, booster caught by the tower in 2024
Starlink: by far the largest satellite constellation ever operated
Launched Europa Clipper for NASA in October 2024

entities.name: ActInSpace
entities.status: every two years — 2026 finals in Bordeaux
entities.does: A 24-hour contest to turn a real space patent into a business idea

entities.name: AI Security Institute
entities.does: State-run evaluations of frontier models for dangerous capabilities

entities.name: AI2
entities.does: Fully open models — weights

entities.name: ALICE
entities.does: Heavy-ion collisions — the quark-gluon plasma that filled the early universe

entities.name: ALPHA
entities.does: Trapped antihydrogen — whether antimatter obeys the same spectroscopy and gravity as matter

entities.name: AMS-02
entities.does: Cosmic ray composition from space — searching for antimatter and dark matter signatures

entities.name: Arc Institute
entities.org: non-profit, with Stanford, UCSF and Berkeley
entities.does: Where AI and biology meet as one lab: genome language models built next to the wet benches that test them.
notable: Its Evo models read and write DNA across all domains of life
Used a genome language model to design working bacteriophages
Funds scientists for years at a time, not grant cycles

entities.name: Astroscale
entities.does: Rendezvous with and removal of dead satellites and debris — the orbital cleanup business
notable: ELSA-d demonstrated magnetic capture of a client satellite in 2021
ADRAS-J flew right up to a discarded Japanese rocket stage in 2024 and photographed it
Working toward actually removing debris, not just approaching it

entities.name: ATLAS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — Higgs properties and searches for new particles
notable: Co-discovered the Higgs boson in 2012
Has published thousands of measurements and searches since
Being rebuilt now for the High-Luminosity LHC

entities.name: Belle II
entities.does: Electron-positron collisions at the Upsilon(4S) — B meson decays and flavour anomalies

entities.name: BioNTech
entities.does: Founded to make cancer immunotherapy, became famous for a vaccine, and has gone back to cancer.
notable: Co-developed the first authorised mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, with Pfizer
Founders Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci started it for cancer, not viruses
Oncology pipeline now includes bispecific antibodies

entities.name: Broad Institute
entities.full_name: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
entities.does: Genomics at industrial scale, and the lab behind base editing and prime editing.
notable: Base and prime editing now in more than 25 clinical trials
gnomAD has contributed to over 13 million genetic diagnoses
Has sequenced nearly 900,000 whole human genomes

entities.name: Caltech SURF
entities.status: annual — proposals due in the winter
entities.does: A summer of research at Caltech or JPL, written up and defended like a real project — students propose the work themselves.
notable: Running since 1979
Students write their own proposal with a mentor
JPL projects are part of the same programme

entities.name: CERN Summer Student
entities.status: annual — applications close in the winter
entities.does: Eight to thirteen weeks on a real project at CERN, with a lecture series alongside it. Paid: a net allowance of 94 CHF per day, health insurance, and travel costs in some cases.
notable: For bachelor's and master's students with at least six semesters done
Physics, engineering, computer science and maths
One of the few places an undergraduate works inside a running experiment

entities.name: CMS
entities.does: General-purpose proton collisions — the independent cross-check on ATLAS

entities.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
entities.does: A compact tokamak made possible by high-temperature superconducting magnets — the magnets are the whole bet.
notable: SPARC is designed to be the first commercially relevant machine to produce net fusion energy
ARC, the power plant meant to follow it, is already sited
The largest private fusion company by funding

entities.name: Copernicus Masters
entities.does: Prizes

entities.name: CRISPR Therapeutics
entities.does: Makes the first approved CRISPR medicine: patients' own stem cells, edited and returned.
notable: Casgevy, developed with Vertex, is approved for sickle cell disease and beta thalassaemia
Co-founded by Emmanuelle Charpentier
The first time gene editing became a prescription

entities.name: DESY Summer Students
entities.does: Seven and a half weeks inside a major accelerator laboratory, on photon science, accelerators, particle or astroparticle physics.
notable: 2026 edition ran 21 July to 10 September
Free hostel accommodation plus a daily stipend, travel partly reimbursed
Open to undergraduates in physics and related fields

entities.name: EleutherAI
entities.does: Grassroots open-source research collective; released open models when almost nobody else did

entities.name: ESA Business Incubation
entities.does: Funding

entities.name: ESA Young Graduate Trainee
entities.does: About 100 one-year paid traineeships a year for people finishing a master's degree

entities.name: Euclid
entities.does: Surveying a third of the sky to map how dark energy stretched the universe
notable: First survey images, November 2023
First bulk data release, 2025 — the survey is meant to run six years

entities.name: Europa Clipper
entities.does: Will fly close passes over Europa to test whether its subsurface ocean could be habitable
notable: Launched October 2024 on a Falcon Heavy
Mars gravity assist, March 2025
Will make dozens of close passes rather than orbit Europa — radiation would kill it

entities.name: Exotrail
entities.does: Electric thrusters and an orbital transfer vehicle — the tow truck that moves satellites
notable: spacevan, an orbital transfer vehicle, has flown
ExoMG Hall thrusters fly on other operators' smallsats
Sells the manoeuvre, not the hardware — mobility as a service

entities.name: FASER
entities.does: Very forward particles — collider neutrinos and long-lived light particles

entities.name: Fervo Energy
entities.does: Geothermal power anywhere hot rock is deep enough, using the horizontal drilling and fibre sensing the oil industry perfected.
notable: Signed a 396 MW power purchase agreement with Google, September 2026
Building Cape Station in Utah
Staffed deliberately with oil and gas engineers

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.does: Gemini
notable: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016
AlphaFold predicted protein structures at scale; its authors shared a Nobel in 2024
Gemini is the production model line

entities.name: Google Summer of Code
entities.does: Twelve weeks contributing to an open-source project with a mentor from that project, stipend included. Several scientific-software organisations take part each year.
notable: Over 21,000 contributors since 2005, across 1,000+ organisations
Astropy, the HEP software projects and similar groups participate regularly
Contact the organisation before the proposal window — that is what decides selection

entities.name: Helion
entities.does: Pulsed magneto-inertial fusion that aims to turn the plasma's energy straight into electricity, skipping the steam turbine.
notable: Polaris: the first privately built machine to show measurable deuterium-tritium fusion
Raised $465 million in June 2026 at a $15.5 billion valuation
Building Orion, which it calls the first fusion power plant

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.does: The public hub where models and datasets are shared — the field's distribution layer

entities.name: IAI Space
entities.does: Observation and communications satellites
notable: Ofek reconnaissance satellites, launched on Israel's own Shavit rocket
The Amos communications satellite series
Built the Beresheet lander with SpaceIL
One of about eleven organisations worldwide with end-to-end space capability

entities.name: ICEYE
entities.does: Small radar satellites that image through cloud and darkness
notable: Put the first smallsat synthetic-aperture radar in orbit
Its flood maps are used by insurers and disaster response
Radar sees through cloud and at night, which optical imaging cannot

entities.name: ICTP Trieste
entities.full_name: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics
entities.does: Schools, workshops and a diploma year in theoretical physics, aimed particularly at scientists from countries without that training at home.
notable: Founded by Abdus Salam to keep physics from concentrating in rich countries
Most schools cover travel and accommodation for accepted participants
Work here fed into neutrino oscillation theory and climate modelling

entities.name: ImageSat International
entities.does: High-resolution observation satellites and the analysis layer on top of them
notable: Operates the EROS high-resolution observation satellites
GEOIMPACT layers AI analysis over the imagery
Sells sovereign capability, not only pictures

entities.name: Intuitive Machines
entities.does: Nova-C lunar landers flown under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme
notable: IM-1 Odysseus, February 2024 — the first US soft landing since Apollo, though it tipped over
IM-2 Athena followed in March 2025
Flies under NASA's commercial lunar payload programme

entities.name: Isomorphic Labs
entities.org: Alphabet, spun out of Google DeepMind
entities.does: AlphaFold's successors, pointed at drug design instead of structure prediction.
notable: Led by Demis Hassabis, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel for AlphaFold
Co-developed AlphaFold 3 with Google DeepMind
Drug-discovery partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies

entities.name: ISS
entities.does: Continuously crewed laboratory — microgravity science and the testbed for everything that follows
notable: Continuously crewed since November 2000
AMS-02 has been mounted outside since 2011
The testbed for every commercial crew and station programme that follows

entities.name: JUICE
entities.does: Will study Ganymede
notable: Launched April 2023
First ever Moon-then-Earth double gravity assist, August 2024
Venus flyby 2025; Jupiter arrival planned 2031

entities.name: KATRIN
entities.does: The neutrino mass directly

entities.name: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
entities.does: Spacetime ripples from merging black holes and neutron stars
notable: GW150914 (2015): the first direct detection, two black holes merging
GW170817 (2017): a neutron star merger seen in gravitational waves and in light
The O4 observing run has pushed the catalogue past 200 candidate events

entities.name: LZ
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — XENONnT's main competitor and cross-check

entities.name: Meta FAIR
entities.does: Open-weight Llama models and a large share of the field's published research

entities.name: Mila
entities.does: One of the largest academic deep learning groups

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.does: Europe's frontier lab

entities.name: Moderna
entities.does: Medicines written as mRNA: instructions the body's own cells follow to make the protein that does the work.
notable: COVID-19 vaccine, 2020
Its mRNA flu vaccine was approved by the FDA in August 2026
Personalised cancer vaccines built from each patient's tumour are in late-stage trials

entities.name: NA62
entities.does: The ultra-rare kaon decay K+ to pi+ nu nubar — one of the sharpest tests of the Standard Model

entities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
entities.does: A weekend hackathon on real agency data; local events run in Israel and across Europe

entities.name: NIF
entities.does: 192 laser beams crush a fuel capsule until it fuses — the only laboratory on Earth to have reached ignition.
notable: December 2022: more fusion energy out than laser energy in, a first anywhere
2.05 MJ of laser light produced 3.1 MJ of fusion yield
Ignition has since been repeated at higher gain

entities.name: Oxford PV
entities.org: private, spun out of Oxford University
entities.does: Perovskite layered on silicon — two cells in one, each catching the part of sunlight the other wastes.
notable: Built on Henry Snaith's perovskite research
Among the first to put perovskite-silicon tandems into commercial modules
Tandems are how solar gets past the single-junction efficiency limit

entities.name: Parker Solar Probe
entities.does: Flying through the Sun's corona to find out what heats it and accelerates the solar wind
notable: First spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, 2021
Closest approach December 2024, about 6.1 million km from the surface
Fastest object ever built by humans

entities.name: Perseverance
entities.does: Roving an ancient river delta and caching samples for a future return mission
notable: Carried Ingenuity, which flew 72 times before its rotor was damaged in 2024
Sample tubes cached at Three Forks, waiting for a return mission
Found organic molecules in Jezero's delta rocks

entities.name: Pierre Auger Observatory
entities.does: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays — where the most energetic particles in nature come from

entities.name: Planet Labs
entities.does: Images the entire landmass of Earth daily with a fleet of small optical satellites
notable: The Dove flock images Earth's entire landmass daily
SkySat adds high-resolution tasking on top of that baseline
Archive now spans more than a decade of daily coverage

entities.name: Ramon Foundation
entities.does: Israel's space education pipeline — school programmes

entities.name: Ramon.Space
entities.does: Radiation-tolerant computers for spacecraft — supercomputing that survives orbit
notable: Radiation-tolerant processors that keep working through orbital radiation
Aimed at moving real computation off the ground and into the spacecraft
Opened US engineering operations near Denver

entities.name: Rocket Lab
entities.does: Electron small launcher
notable: Electron reached orbit in 2018 and is the busiest small launcher
Launched CAPSTONE to lunar orbit for NASA in 2022
Recovers boosters from the sea to study reuse
Neutron, a larger reusable vehicle, is in development

entities.name: Rubin Observatory
entities.does: Will image the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
notable: First-look images released June 2025
Will repeat the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years
Expected to multiply the number of known solar system objects

entities.name: SolarEdge
entities.does: The electronics between a solar panel and the grid — optimisers and inverters that get more out of every roof.
notable: Installed in more than 140 countries
Leads in rooftop solar capacity
Moved into home storage and grid services

entities.name: StemRad
entities.does: The AstroRad vest
notable: AstroRad flew on Artemis I around the Moon, on the MARE experiment
Also tested aboard the ISS
Shields bone marrow selectively rather than the whole body

entities.name: StoreDot
entities.does: Silicon-anode batteries built to charge an electric car in minutes rather than hours.
notable: Extreme-fast-charging cells at 300 Wh/kg
Partnerships with Mercedes, Volvo and Polestar
Backed by bp and TDK

entities.name: T2K
entities.does: Neutrino oscillation and hints of CP violation in the lepton sector

entities.name: TerraPower
entities.does: Natrium, a sodium-cooled fission reactor with molten-salt storage bolted on — so the plant can surge when the grid needs it.
notable: First plant under construction in Wyoming
345 MWe, with over five hours of molten-salt energy storage
Also developing medical isotopes for cancer treatment

entities.name: Voyager 1 and 2
entities.does: The only working instruments humanity has outside the Sun's bubble
notable: Voyager 1 crossed into interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018
Engineers recovered Voyager 1 from a failed memory chip in 2024, from 24 billion km away
Instruments are being switched off one by one to stretch the power budget

entities.name: Weizmann Institute
entities.does: One of the world's leading basic-science institutes, strong in immunology, cancer and the gut microbiome.
notable: Its ILLUMINE team won up to £20m in Cancer Grand Challenges, 2025
Pioneering work linking gut microbes to immunity
Research here led to several of Israel's best-known drugs

entities.name: Wendelstein 7-X
entities.org: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
entities.does: The largest stellarator ever built — a twisted magnetic bottle designed to hold plasma continuously rather than in pulses.
notable: First plasma in December 2015; 50 superconducting coils, none of them a simple shape
Built to sustain discharges up to 30 minutes
Reaches confinement comparable to tokamaks without their pulsed limit

entities.name: XENONnT
entities.does: Direct dark matter detection — a WIMP recoiling off a liquid xenon nucleus

entities.name: XRISM
entities.does: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy — the motion of hot gas around black holes and clusters
notable: Resolve spectrometer reads gas motion around black holes to a few km/s
First science results released 2024

canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor
canon.why: How hot, how dense and for how long — the bar every fusion machine is still measured against.

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
canon.why: One page, and the double helix. Built on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data, which she was not told they had.

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
canon.why: Quantum mechanics turned into the chemist's everyday picture of bonds and hybrid orbitals.

canon.title: A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae
canon.why: Two and a half pages showing the universe is expanding. Cosmology starts here.

watch.name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
watch.why: Nine lectures building a working GPT from nothing, in code, with every line explained.

watch.name: Neural networks
watch.why: The visual explanation of what a network is actually doing. Start here if the maths looks opaque.

watch.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
watch.why: Top-down: you train a working model in lesson one and learn why it worked afterwards.

watch.name: Short courses (agents, RAG, evaluation)
watch.why: Short, current, built with the labs themselves — though the catalogue has moved to a membership.

watch.name: Paper walkthroughs
watch.why: Reads the week's papers out loud and argues with them, which is how you learn to read them yourself.

watch.name: PBS Space Time
watch.why: The rare channel that keeps the real equations in and still stays followable.

watch.name: Dr. Becky
watch.why: A working astrophysicist walking through the month's results, including the ones that did not hold up.

watch.name: Fermilab
watch.why: Particle physics explained by the lab that does it, without the press-release gloss.

watch.name: Cool Worlds
watch.why: A working exoplanet astronomer thinking out loud about habitability and how we would ever know.

watch.name: Anton Petrov
watch.why: A short, careful video on almost every new astronomy result, usually within days of the paper.

watch.name: Kurzgesagt
watch.why: The most beautiful science animation being made, and the sources are published alongside each video.

watch.name: Deep Sky Videos
watch.why: Real astronomers talking through objects one at a time, telescope time included.

watch.name: Event Horizon
watch.why: Long interviews with the researchers themselves — where cosmology arguments actually get made.

watch.name: Scott Manley
watch.why: Orbital mechanics and launch failures explained by someone who reads the telemetry.

watch.name: Astrum
watch.why: Built from real probe imagery — what the spacecraft actually sent back, not an artist's impression.

books.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
books.who: Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari and Rubin
books.why: How to reason about uncertainty when you have a model and not much data. Free PDF from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Recipes
books.why: The algorithms behind the library functions you call, explained well enough to know when they will fail you.

books.title: Statistical Data Analysis
books.why: The standard reference for how physicists actually handle errors, fits and limits. Short, and nothing wasted.

books.title: Data Reduction and Error Analysis for the Physical Sciences
books.why: The first statistics book most physics students meet, and the one they keep going back to.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.why: If you are going to publish plots, read this before you publish more of them.

books.title: An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics
books.why: The standard undergraduate course in one very heavy volume — stars, galaxies, cosmology, all of it.

books.title: Introduction to Cosmology
books.why: The clearest first cosmology book there is. You can read it end to end without getting stuck.

books.title: Black Holes and Time Warps
books.why: Written before LIGO detected anything, by the person who argued it would. Worth reading for that alone.

books.title: The First Three Minutes
books.why: A Nobel laureate walking through the early universe minute by minute, without hiding the physics.

books.title: Liftoff
books.why: How SpaceX nearly died before Falcon 1 reached orbit. Reported, not mythologised.

books.title: Reentry
books.why: The sequel: Falcon 9, reuse, and the decisions that turned a survivor into the whole market.

books.title: Space Mission Analysis and Design
books.why: The engineering reference the industry actually sizes missions with. Known simply as SMAD.

books.title: The Right Stuff
books.why: Why anyone climbs onto a rocket at all. Still the best writing about test pilots and nerve.

books.title: Modern Particle Physics
books.why: The current standard course. Works the calculations through instead of quoting results.

books.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
books.why: Griffiths explains things the way a good supervisor would. Start here before Thomson.

books.title: Review of Particle Physics
books.why: Every measured property of every known particle, updated yearly and free. The field's single most-used document.

books.title: Lost in Math
books.why: An argument that beauty has been a bad guide in theoretical physics. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Plasma Physics and Fusion Energy
books.why: What it would actually take to build a fusion reactor, with the engineering constraints left in.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.why: A Pulitzer for a book that is also a genuine history of 20th-century nuclear physics. Read it for Meitner and Bohr.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.why: Reactor physics as it behaves when institutions fail. The clearest account of what actually happened.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The foundations, from linear algebra up. Free online, and still the reference for why things work.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Bridges classical statistics and deep learning in one framework. Draft PDF free, code in Python and JAX.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: By the people who built the field. Free PDF, and still the clearest treatment of the basics.

books.title: The Alignment Problem
books.why: The honest version of why making these systems do what we meant is hard, told through the research.

books.title: Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air
books.why: Every energy argument turned into kilowatt-hours per person per day. Free online, and it settles a lot of arguments.

books.title: Molecular Biology of the Cell
books.why: The textbook of cell biology. If you come from physics, this is where the vocabulary comes from.

books.title: The Gene
books.why: From Mendel to gene editing, written by an oncologist with a family history that makes it personal.

books.title: The Code Breaker
books.why: Jennifer Doudna and the race to CRISPR, with the rivalries left in.

books.title: The Emperor of All Maladies
books.why: A biography of cancer. Won the Pulitzer, and explains why the mRNA cancer vaccines matter so much.

items.title: Dark-Matter-Induced Nuclear Deexcitation at the Short-Baseline Near Detector with Ab Initio Nuclear Theory

items.abstract: We explore the sensitivity of the short-baseline near detector (SBND) experiment to light dark matter using MeV-scale electromagnetic activity. Inelastic scattering of dark matter with argon nuclei can excite nuclear states that subsequently deexcite via the emission of MeV-scale photons, producing localized low-energy “blip” signatures in a liquid argon time projection chamber. We perform state-of-the-art nuclear calculations, including all relevant argon excited states with energies up to 18 MeV, to provide reliable predictions for these signals. After accounting for relevant backgrounds, we find that SBND can probe previously unexplored regions of parameter space for light dark matter.

items.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

items.title: The Hot Neptune Initiative (HONEI): IV. TOI-4129 b, an Adolescent Neptune in the Ridge
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Recent exoplanet demographics studies have uncovered the Neptune ridge: an overdensity of intermediate-size planets at orbital periods between 3--6~d. The origin of this pile-up remains unclear, but it could be a consequence of high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Here, we confirm TOI-4129\,b, a planet that may help to reveal the origin of the Neptune ridge. Using radial velocities from HARPS-N and transit photometry from TESS and four ground-based telescopes, we found that TOI-4129\,b has a relatively low density ($R_p = 5.7 \pm 0.2\, R_\oplus$, $M_p = 26\pm 6 \,M_\oplus$, $ρ_p = 0.8 \pm 0.2 ~\textrm{g}~\textrm{cm}^{-3}$) and orbits a $V = 12.9$ K dwarf star every 3.27~d, placing it at the inner edge of the Neptune ridge. We detect the stellar rotation period at 12.7~d in the photometry, implying a fairly young gyrochronal age of $1.20^{+0.16}_{-0.30}~$Gyr for the system. With a Transmission Spectroscopy Metric of $112\pm 30$, this adolescent Neptune is a good target for atmospheric observations with \textit{JWST} and \textit{Ariel}, and we also find that it is amenable to future constraints on the (three-dimensional) stellar obliquity. TOI-4129\,b will therefore be an important testing ground for the idea that planets in the Neptune ridge underwent HEM to arrive at their current locations.

items.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $γ$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $γ$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $γ$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2σ$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $γ$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

items.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Periodic flux modulations may arise from the orbital motion of black holes in close binaries, while relativistic jet precession can provide an additional source of periodic variability. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. For a total mass of $10^{8.95} M_\odot$ and a mass ratio q = 0.1, the derived milli-parsec separation and a short gravitational wave driven coalescence time, $t_c = 1122^{+144}_{-144}$ years, imply that PKS 0301-243 may be a rare source of nano-hertz gravitational waves and a potential multimessenger laboratory for the terminal stages of supermassive black hole coalescence.

items.title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Quantum-mechanical interaction potentials support localized bound states below the dissociation threshold or delocalized scattering states above it. Although bound states are energetically isolated, scattering states couple a quantum system to environmental modes, making dissipation and loss intrinsic to open systems. Bound states in the continuum are an exception, as destructive interference keeps them localized within the scattering continuum. Theory predicts that such states can arise through interference between two Feshbach resonances coupled to a common continuum. Here we form such an interference-stabilized state in ultracold collisions of 6 Li atoms by coherently coupling two tunable Feshbach resonances using Floquet engineering. At a critical parameter point, elastic and inelastic coupling to the continuum vanish, producing a molecular state above the dissociation threshold. Consequently, resonant scattering features disappear and the colliding atoms become effectively transparent to one another. Full coupled-channel calculations and a minimal non-Hermitian model quantitatively reproduce our observations and identify the state as a Friedrich–Wintgen bound state in the continuum. These results show how quantum interference can control openness in quantum matter and enable the engineering of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

items.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.

items.title: Hydrogen Electron Cyclotron Resonance Dissociator Demonstrator for the Project 8 Experiment
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. Our pioneering experiment will consist of a beamline that dissociates molecular tritium, surface cools atoms through accommodation, evaporatively cools and slows atoms, and traps them in a CRES resonant cavity to advance towards our sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2 for our final electron-weighted neutrino mass measurement. We are prototyping an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) dissociator that uses a tunable 1 kW 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a hydrogen plasma in an aluminum resonant cavity. Our ECR source is designed to produce a high atom flux (~10^19 atoms/second) near room temperature. We present the engineering development, gas diagnostics, and spectroscopy data from our hydrogen plasma.

items.title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features—one that enhances and one that suppresses activity—around an elevated baseline firing rate. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. items.title: Construction and performance evaluation of a meter-scale monolithic scintillator tracker with embedded scatterers
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: A meter-scale Fiber-Readout mOnolithic and Scatterer-embedded scintillator Tracker (FROST) was constructed and operated in the NINJA experiment to enable muon-track matching between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. The detector consists of a 1.32 m $\times$ 1.40 m plastic scintillator plate assembled from optically bonded scatterer-embedded plates, with wavelength-shifting fibers arranged at a pitch of 10 mm. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation, FROST achieved a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946$\pm$0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area. A position reconstruction method based on the light-yield distribution was developed for both single- and multi-particle events. In a neutrino-interaction simulation, muon position resolutions of 1.77 mm and 1.61 mm were achieved in the two orthogonal readout directions, assuming correct muon identification. Using a beam-data sample dominated by single-muon events, upper limits on the position resolution of 2.20 mm and 2.03 mm were obtained for track angles below 20°. These results demonstrate that the FROST concept can be scaled up to a meter-scale active area while maintaining high detection efficiency and a position resolution well below the readout pitch under actual experimental conditions.

items.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to π^+π^-(γ)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$Υ(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $π^+π^-$ to $μ^+μ^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

items.title: A New Precise Measurement of the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We measure the $e^+e^-\toπ^+π^-(γ)$ cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb$^{-1}$ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the $π^+π^-/μ^+μ^-$ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV is $a_μ^{ππ}=525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

items.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour 1–5 . However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

items.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment 1–8 , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear 9–13 . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

items.title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

items.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

items.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child’s natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child’s ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child’s learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

items.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

items.title: Symbolic Quantum-Trajectory Method for Multichannel Dicke Superradiance
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: We solve Dicke superradiance with two or more competing collective decay channels of tunable rates using a symbolic quantum-trajectory construction. The method yields closed time-domain populations and observables as finite combinations of exponential terms for arbitrary numbers of emitters and arbitrary decay rates. For two channels, the behavior of the stationary ground-state distribution resembles a first-order phase transition at the point where the channel-rate ratio is equal to unity. For balanced d -channel decay, we obtain scaling laws for the superradiant peak time and intensity. These results unify and extend single-channel Dicke dynamics to multilevel emitters and provide a compact tool for cavity and waveguide experiments, where permutation-symmetric reservoirs engineer multiple collective decay paths.

items.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision. A single request can launch calculations for an entire collection of molecules, without requiring a separate LLM decision for every compound. This design limits the information the model must process as screening collections grow, while keeping the underlying results available for inspection and further analysis. The integrated tools support molecule generation, prediction of binding and molecular properties, and searches for compounds available for purchase. In a retrospective comparison with an expert-led campaign, the agent proposed chemically distinct candidates with competitive docking scores and higher calculated drug-likeness under explicitly imposed selection criteria. In a 22-task benchmark against plain tool calls and Codex, the agent achieved the highest observed mean model-judged score, with lower median cumulative token use and peak context. Fármaco provides a foundation for flexible, scalable drug discovery workflows that connect scientific reasoning with an enduring, traceable record of computational work.

items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the ‘fight-or-flight’ response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) – an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. Transcriptome analyses indicated that SBV infections, and DWV infection with OA treatment, activated honey bee metabolic pathways, and that SBV-infected bees had greater expression of genes involved in OA synthesis, unless treated with OA. items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". The dataset PigAirwayPressure is not an outlier. Although the archive is the standard benchmark, whether its tasks resemble the problems TSC is meant to solve has rarely been examined. We find that several datasets are repurposed from their original task, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits. We further question how representative the archive's ordered non-temporal sequences (e.g. spectra, shape outlines) are of real TSC, and the potential downsides from the decomposition of multivariate problems. Our findings call for more careful interpretation of archive-wide scores and greater attention to deployment-relevant evaluation. The audit is at https://github.com/automl/ucr-provenance-audit.

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. To study how best to use monitors to mitigate reward hacking, we introduce and open source three realistic environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks: a coding environment hackable via test overwriting, a medical chat environment hackable via sycophancy, and a biography generation environment hackable via hallucination. We first focus on the coding environment, where we find that: (1) models can learn to evade highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic flaws in probes and LLM judges; (2) monitors that leak more learning signal during RL suppress reward hacking but are more often evaded; and (3) including easier problems in training can decrease reward hacking. We apply our findings to build better reward hacking monitors for the medical chat and biography generation environments that improve upon naive baselines to reduce reward hacking rates across seeds to before-training levels in some interventions. Our results demonstrate that our takeaways translate to new settings and that better monitor intervention designs are possible.

items.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: LLM-based coding agents such as Claude Code are guided by repository instruction files (also called context files or agent configuration files) like AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which are read in every agent session. As any documentation artifact, these files can fall behind the code and become stale (e.g., a test folder moves, but the file still points to the old one). In technical debt terms, such a stale instruction is documentation debt, and its interest is the cost it adds to every later agent session. Evaluations that check only task success can miss this cost, and the stale file can persist. In this study, we ask what leads agents to act on a stale instruction, how it affects their behavior and at what cost, and how they recover. We study three real-world stale instructions from active open-source repositories in depth, each a different kind of guidance: a test command, a code location, and a procedure for adding a component. Agents fix 22 maintenance tasks under three versions of each instruction (left stale, corrected to the current path, and removed), with the code and the task held fixed, and we analyze 732 trajectories of two models at the level of individual tool calls. We find that agents follow stale guidance when it is relevant to their tasks, sometimes even when correct information is available elsewhere. On the stale test command, Claude Sonnet 5.5 needed about two extra tool calls per run, a third more than with the corrected command; in the other cases, we could not detect a difference. Although agents generally recovered from the immediate failures, none repaired the underlying instruction file. Correcting the instructions eliminated operations on obsolete paths, while removing them prevented most. Our findings show that task success alone can hide the costs of documentation debt, highlighting the need to evaluate agent behavior beyond final outcomes.

items.title: Are the tearing and the Weibel instabilities the same?
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The tearing instability, which extracts free energy from a magnetic field gradient, and the Weibel instability, which draws free energy from temperature anisotropies, appear at first glance to be fundamentally distinct. However, the magnetic field gradient in the tearing instability requires a current, and the resulting plasma drift leads to an effective temperature anisotropy, so that the plasma is hotter along the direction of the current flow. This anisotropy can play an essential role in driving the instability. We demonstrate, using semi-implicit particle-in-cell simulations, a smooth transition between the tearing regime for thick current sheets, where the anisotropy has little influence, and a thin-current-sheet regime better described by Weibel physics. We find that for current sheet thicknesses less than the ion Larmor radius, where standard assumptions of the tearing instability break down, the growth rate of the mode commonly identified as the tearing instability agrees remarkably well with the growth rate predicted by ion-cyclotron theory, which is essentially the magnetized counterpart of the Weibel instability.

items.title: Suppression of the Laser Hosing Instability in a Parabolic Plasma Channel
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We present an analytical stability analysis of the laser hosing instability in a parabolic channel in the weakly relativistic regime. We employ a variational principle approach to derive a set of coupled equations describing laser dynamics in a transversely inhomogeneous plasma. The quadratic Lagrangian formalism is applied to perform a stability analysis and to derive the growth rates for hosing in both long- and short-wavelength regimes. We find that a parabolic channel suppresses the long-wavelength hosing mode completely, for any channel depth, and that the unstable band of the short-wavelength mode is bounded below by a cutoff wavenumber set by the ratio of the channel frequency to the hosing coupling. A steeper channel narrows the unstable band and lowers the short-wavelength growth rate, but cannot stabilize the mode, since the dispersion relation forbids damping identically. The analysis is accompanied by two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, which reproduce the prediction in the nonlinear regime: the long-wavelength mode is absent in a channel, the surviving modulation shortens as the channel steepens, and its amplitude falls with channel depth. Further, our simulation results demonstrate the sensitivity of off-axis laser propagation to the plasma channel and distinguish the hosing instability from laser oscillations due to off-axis laser propagation in a plasma channel.

items.title: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Sample-based quantum subspace methods construct a small subspace from measured basis states and solve the target problem classically within it. We study these methods for heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where the anisotropy $χ_\parallel/χ_\perp$ reaches $10^8$ to $10^{10}$. We prove two results for the energy-norm Galerkin solution. First, if the measurement basis is aligned with the flux surfaces and the subspace contains the poloidal-mode-zero block, the error is bounded by $\|r_0\|_{L^+}(χ_\parallel-χ_\perp)^{-1/2}$, where the numerator does not depend on $χ_\parallel$. The bound is sharp, so the accuracy improves as the anisotropy grows. Second, in the computational basis, a subspace that misses a single node of a flux surface suppresses the flux-function component there as $χ_\parallel^{-1/2}$, which gives an error floor when the limiting solution is nonzero on that surface. We verify both results on a shaped cross-section and on a KSTAR-like Miller equilibrium with ten qubits. At $χ_\parallel/χ_\perp=10^9$, the computational basis gives an error of order unity for every shot budget, whereas a quantum Fourier transform on the poloidal register gives $1.3\times10^{-5}$. The same barrier limits sample-based quantum diagonalization. The aligned measurement needs no time evolution, so the circuit is only state preparation and a five-qubit quantum Fourier transform. On a ten-qubit superconducting processor, the aligned basis gives a median error of $7.0\times10^{-6}$ with 768 shots, whereas the computational basis gives errors above 0.94 up to $1.2\times10^4$ shots. A trapped-ion processor shows the same behavior.

items.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.

items.title: Emotion knowledge is structured in a grid-like coordinate system in the human ventromedial prefrontal cortex
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Yumeng Ma, Philip A. Kragel Human emotional experiences vary widely in everyday life, yet they are systematically organized within a continuous affective space defined by valence and arousal. Although this circumplex organization has shaped decades of research, its neural implementation remains unclear. Here, we asked whether abstract emotion concepts are encoded using grid-like coordinate principles in the human brain. During fMRI, participants tracked trajectories through affective space conveyed through morphs of facial expressions and sequences of phrases. We found that ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) encoded affective space with robust hexadirectional modulation characteristic of grid-like coding. This coordinate representation generalized across stimulus modalities, indicating abstraction beyond perceptual features. The grid-like signal reflected a metric organization of emotion concepts independent of overt behavior, whereas distance-related signals in vmPFC predicted trial-by-trial affective judgements. Together, these findings suggest that emotion knowledge is structured by a grid-like coordinate system in the human brain that can support predictive inference and flexible decision-making.

items.title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: One aspect of pangenome analysis that has received little attention is the recovery of the individual genomes that gave rise to a pangenome graph. While substantial effort has focused on constructing pangenomes from collections of genomes, the inverse problem remains largely unexplored: given a pangenome represented as a set of weighted adjacencies, can we reconstruct the constituent linear genomes that underlie it? Thus we introduce the pangenome peeling problem, which seeks to decompose a weighted adjacency graph into a collection of linear genomes whose combined adjacencies reproduce the observed edge weights. This problem is particularly relevant when considering ancestral pangenomes, where the graph structure may be known or inferred, but the underlying genomes are not. As a first step toward addressing this problem, we formally define pangenome peeling and derive a lower bound on the minimum number of genomes required to explain a given weighted adjacency graph. We then present two reconstruction methods: one based on the sequential addition of edges and a second based on extracting maximum-spanning-tree structures. Both methods produce genome collections that exactly explain the input adjacency data. To evaluate the recovered sets of genomes, we compare them to the set of input genomes using a maximum-weight matching framework based on the double-cut-and-join distance with indels. Here the maximum-spanning tree approach is superior, producing sets of constituent genomes close to the simulations while the sequential addition of edges approach yields constituent genomes increasingly divergent from the input as genomes sizes increase.

items.title: Ten simple rules for a department chair
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Lubomir Tomaska Department chairs occupy a pivotal position in the university. Teaching, research, graduate education, and much of the academic community's professional and administrative activity are organized at the departmental level. Yet, despite the importance of the position and the considerable challenges it entails, many scientists assume the role with little or no formal preparation for academic leadership. This paper is intended as a practical primer rather than a comprehensive guide to academic leadership. The proposed rules provide a framework that prospective and current department chairs can adapt to their own institutional circumstances, experience, and leadership style.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and Chinese art teachers’ career exploration behavior: The roles of job substitution risks, job insecurity, and organizational AI readiness
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (verified on article pages; occasional CC0)
items.abstract: by Jia Li, Yun Gao The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers’ professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption–career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.

items.title: Protein B-factor modeling with local magnitude
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Topological magnitude characterizes the effective size and spatial organization of metric spaces, offering a geometric approach with potential applications in molecular biology and materials science. Previous work has demonstrated its utility in modeling protein flexibility from structure, but global magnitude weighting requires dense linear systems whose computational cost increases with protein size. We introduce a local magnitude representation that retains residue-level structural information through nearest-neighbor environments. The construction is well posed and geometrically invariant, with central weighting distinguished from scalar neighborhood magnitude. Across 364 proteins, the mean within-protein fitting Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) increases from 0.725 for global magnitude to 0.728 for local magnitude. Blind-prediction experiments on 345 proteins combine each representation with identical auxiliary descriptors and evaluate random forests and gradient boosting under three validation protocols. Local features improve the primary PCC in all six model--protocol comparisons, with a maximum absolute increase of 0.008 in protein-level ten-fold gradient boosting. For a fixed feature bank, local factorization costs $O(Nk^3)$ compared with $O(N^3)$ for global factorization, where $N$ is the number of C$_α$ atoms and $k$ the neighborhood size. Timing measurements show a computational advantage of local magnitude on large structures. Within the tested single-seed configuration and distinct global and local scale banks, these results support local magnitude as a compact representation that preserves useful B-factor information while reducing feature-extraction costs for large proteins.
